title: Ground Electronics Systems Maintenance Technician (GySgt to SSgt) PMOS, DIR IC4
raw_text:
8. MOS 2862, Ground Electronics Systems Maintenance Technician (GySgt to
SSgt) PMOS, DIR IC4

    a. Summary. Ground Electronics Systems Maintenance Technicians are
qualified to perform complex diagnosis, field level repairs, and
modifications to ground electronics systems. These technicians supervise
ground electronics systems maintenance activities and instruct in the use and
maintenance of ground electronics communications systems. These technicians



                                        3-257                        Enclosure (1)
 3124                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



provide subject matter expertise in the diagnosis and repair of complex
system and system of systems restoration across the spectrum of ground
electronics to include but not limited to: Ground common transmission
systems, troposcatter, digital fires situational awareness systems, vehicle
intercommunications systems, vehicle electronics equipment, Position,
Navigation, and Timing electronic systems, electronic jamming systems, Marine
Corps Information and Communication Technology systems and transmissions
mediums, End User Devices (EUD), live and recorded broadcasting technologies,
telephony, wired and wireless network devices, optical transmissions systems,
intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) processing systems,
digital wideband communications equipment used for high capacity, and
satellite link communications, nonstandard equipment, and miscellaneous non-
communication systems, electro-mechanical devices to include, but not limited
to unmanned, robotic, and multi-function systems involving motors, servos,
actuators and their control systems and components at organizational and
intermediate maintenance activities. Typical duties include complex field
level repairs and modifications to ground electronics systems, supervision of
a maintenance section or shop, coordination of equipment evacuation for
repair with other maintenance activities, enforcing quality control measures
and effective management of the maintenance cycle to include requisitioning
of parts, monitoring maintenance reports and the management of internal shop
programs. These technicians also provide technical assistance during the
employment and installation of data/radio/satellite communication systems.
This MOS is career progression for MOSs 2831, 2841 and 2847. MOS 2862 is
assigned upon completion of the Electronics Maintenance Technician Course
(M09DSM1). Marines in this MOS may be assigned to a BIC (within their
occupational field) that has been coded with one or more DoD Cyber Workforce
Framework (DCWF) work role codes. Please reference DoDI 8140.10, DoDM
8140.10, and the MOS roadmap for additional training and certification
requirements associated with these work role codes.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

            (2) This is career progression for MOSs 2831, 2841, and 2847.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Electronics Maintenance Technician Course (M09DSM1)
at MCCES 29 Palms, CA.

        (2) Marines must obtain 24 months of obligated service prior to
reporting into the Electronics Maintenance Technician Course and 24 months of
obligated service remaining upon graduation.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (q), 2800 Ground Electronics Maintenance Training and Readiness
Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Radio Mechanics 49-2021.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

common_text: The Ground Electronics Maintenance Occupational Field includes the installation, inspection and classification, servicing, adjustment, tuning, repair, modification, recovery and evacuation, overhauling and rebuilding, and testing and calibration of electronic equipment and systems used by Marine Corps ground forces. The equipment includes various types of communications transmission systems, information technology systems, intelligence processing systems, tactical sensor systems, cryptographic devices, artillery electronics systems, digital fire control systems, unmanned vessel electronics, miscellaneous non-communication systems, robotic and various electro-mechanical systems, electronic jamming systems, and a wide range of test equipment and calibration required devices. Qualifications to work in this field include manual dexterity, normal color vision, be eligible to hold a secret security clearance, the ability to understand highly technical material, and to comprehend complex mathematical and logic principles. Types of entry-level jobs available include work as a Ground Electronics Transmission Systems Maintainer, Ground Electronics Telecommunications and Information Technology Systems Maintainer, Calibration Technician, Artillery Electronics Technician, and Digital Wideband Systems Maintainer. Formal schooling is provided to all Marines entering this field. In general, entry-level training consists of basic electronics, electronic systems fundamentals, and an equipment-oriented phase at either a Marine Corps school or other service school. Career progression training will involve related supervisory/technical level training within the field. Skill progression, skill enhancement and skill sustainment training is provided via on the job training and through both distributed learning and formal schooling. Billets for ground electronics maintenance are found throughout the Marine Corps but are concentrated within units having specific electronic or service support missions. Marines in this field may serve within GCE, ACE, MLG, MIG units and supporting establishments. Instructor billets are found at the formal schools responsible for ground electronics training. Marines entering this field will be assigned MOS 2800, Basic Ground Electronics Maintenance Marine.

matches: Modify, maintain, or repair electronics equipment or systems to ensure proper functioning.

The Ground Electronics Maintenance Occupational Field includes the installation, inspection and classification, servicing, adjustment, tuning, repair, modification, recovery and evacuation, overhauling and rebuilding, and testing and calibration of electronic equipment and systems used by Marine Corps ground forces.

Types of entry-level jobs available include work as a Ground Electronics Transmission Systems Maintainer, Ground Electronics Telecommunications and Information Technology Systems Maintainer, Calibration Technician, Artillery Electronics Technician, and Digital Wideband Systems Maintainer.
Supervise or train other technologists, technicians, or drafters.
Career progression training will involve related supervisory/technical level training within the field.
Install, service, and repair electronic equipment or instruments such as televisions, radios, and videocassette recorders.
Billets for ground electronics maintenance are found throughout the Marine Corps but are concentrated within units having specific electronic or service support missions.
Instructor billets are found at the formal schools responsible for ground electronics training.
Modify, maintain, or repair electronics equipment or systems to ensure proper functioning.
Ground Electronics Systems Maintenance Technicians are qualified to perform complex diagnosis, field level repairs, and modifications to ground electronics systems.
These technicians supervise ground electronics systems maintenance activities and instruct in the use and maintenance of ground electronics communications systems.
Provide technical assistance to installers, technicians, or other solar professionals in areas such as solar electric systems, solar thermal systems, electrical systems, or mechanical systems.
These technicians also provide technical assistance during the employment and installation of data/radio/satellite communication systems.
Perform maintenance tasks necessary to keep equipment working properly.
For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (q), 2800 Ground Electronics Maintenance Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
